doc.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023

title: His pop symphony project
summary: Malone arranged orchestral pop hits for a symphony with rhythm section and tells of a fundraiser at North Texas.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: And my recent project is that I arranged a pop symphony act for myself. It’s a symphony orchestra with a rhythm section. And the concept is orchestral pop hits of the twentieth century. Stuff like “MacArthur Park,” “Unforgettable,” “Georgia On My Mind,” “Kashmir,” “Bet You By Golly Wow,” you know, “Philadelphia Sound.” And the average listener doesn’t realize, they just hear their song and they like it or don’t like it, but the average person doesn’t really know whether their hit song that they like was recorded with an orchestra or not. But I do, and I try to put this together, and I’ve done four concerts so far. The most successful one I think was a fundraiser at the University of North Texas at the big Murchison Hall. A big fundraiser. And so the after party, there’s this slightly older patron lady that comes up to me and says she’d enjoyed the music. And I said, “Thank you, did you recognize any of the songs I played?” She said, “I knew the words to every song you played.” I just basically played the melody on these male vocals.

But that’s the audience I’m trying to reach because people are not going out to the symphony to hear the Bach, Beethoven, Mozart, Brahms, Debussy, all that stuff. I love all that music. You know I play symphony gigs too but not as much as jazz and pop gigs. But yeah, so they have to do pop music in order to keep themselves financially sound.
